# 172 — give the STATIC-page prescan a link signal (`link-target-integrity` on generated HTML)

**Risk tier: HIGH** (builder's guess, verifier assigns independently: 242+279 = 521 raw insertions across
two files, well over the 150-line LOW cap, and three sub-rules with three non-vacuity cycles per the
spec's own "when in doubt → HIGH" note). NEVER list clean: no trust rail moved, no product file/generator/
generated page/sitemap/OG asset/dependency touched.

Full build notes: `specs/172-notes.md`. Spec: `specs/172.md`.

---

## The goal, in one sentence

Give `prescanStaticPages()` — the audit's pass over all 2,181 generated `tokens/*.html` + `chains/*.html`
SEO leaf pages — a signal that can see a **link**, because right now it can't see one at all.

## The intuition

`prescanStaticPages()` had four signals: `junk-slug`, `zero-yield-claim`, `broken-number-literal`,
`absurd-magnitude`. Read them again — every single one is a check on a **number or a slug**. Not one of
them ever looks at an `href`. That's not an oversight so much as a pattern: each signal was specced from
the last bug someone got bitten by (148's junk pages → 157's prescan → 159's APY bug → 160's text-surface
twin → 166's link bug → 169's `link-target-integrity` for the TWO text surfaces). Item 169 explicitly
scoped HTML out — "one surface family per item" — leaving the **1,000×-larger** surface, the one that
actually carries SEO traffic, with zero link coverage.

Why that matters concretely: every token/chain page's whole job is to walk a reader through one hop —
`/tokens/<slug>` → `/?pool=<id>` → the two north-star CTAs. This item's own measurement counted **~41,300**
same-origin links doing that job, **4,989** of them `?pool=` links into pool-detail, and **zero** gates
that had ever checked any of them actually addressed a pool, stayed inside the router's known params, or
pointed at a file that exists.

## What was actually measured (before writing a line of code)

| | count |
|---|---|
| generated leaf pages scanned by `prescanStaticPages()` | **2,181** (see Deviation 1 below re: the spec's "2,183") |
| same-origin links they emit | **~41,300** |
| `?pool=<id>` links into pool-detail | **4,989** |
| `a.tp-pool-link`/`a.cp-pool-link` anchors, `?pool=`-targeted | 4,526/4,526, **100%** |
| broken internal page targets (path → no file on disk) | **0** |

The surface is healthy today under all three rules this item ships. That is the point, not a
disappointment: this item ships a **gate**, not a repair — its value is catching the *next* regression,
the way 166 caught the class 169 then automated.

## What changed, in reading order

**1. One new signal, `'link-target-integrity': 'P1'`, added to `PRESCAN_SIGNALS`.** The only edited line
among the four pre-existing signals — an addition to the object literal (it needed a trailing comma to
gain a new sibling key). Their four detection blocks inside `prescanStaticPages()` are untouched,
confirmed by `git diff` (only 5 lines removed across the whole file, all accounted for — see the notes).

**2. A new block of pure helpers**, inserted between `extractPageText()` and `prescanStaticPages()` (so
strictly *before* the function, touching nothing inside it): entity decoding (`decodeHrefEntities`),
owned-link classification (`ownedHtmlLinkSuffix`/`ownedLinkPath` — absolute `https://(www.)?defi.garden/...`
or root-relative `/...`, nothing else), the planner's own allow-list reader (`loadPlannerAllowedParams`),
pool-row address validation (`isPoolAddressingSuffix`), anchor-tag attribute extraction
(`anchorAttr`/`anchorHasClass`, order-independent), and on-disk file resolution
(`ownedPathResolvesToFile`).

**3. Three sub-rules inside `prescanStaticPages()`'s existing per-page loop**, appended strictly after the
four pre-existing signal blocks, running on the RAW `html` string the loop already read (never on
`visibleText` — `extractPageText()` strips every tag, so hrefs are already gone by the time it returns):

| rule | asks | mechanism |
|---|---|---|
| **(a)** unrouted query key | is every query key on every owned link inside its path's allowed set? | path `/` → `home.html`'s `ANALYTICS_PARAMS ∪ PLANNER_PARAMS ∪ {lang}` (169's own `loadRouterAllowedParams()`, reused verbatim); path `/plan.html` → `planner.js`'s own `urlParams.get()` call sites (new: `loadPlannerAllowedParams()`); any other path → skipped, inert |
| **(b)** pool row → non-addressing target | does a `tp-pool-link`/`cp-pool-link` anchor (item 029's classes) target `?pool=<id>`? | bare origin, `?token=`/`?chain=` grid URL, or missing/empty `href` are all suspects |
| **(c)** internal target does not exist | does every other owned link's path resolve to a real file? | checks `<path>`, `<path>.html`, `<path>/index.html` under `ROOT` |

Rules (a) and (c) share one `matchAll(HTML_HREF_RE)` pass (both key off the identical owned-suffix/path
split); rule (b) is a separate pass over `<a ...>` tags since it needs the tag's own `class` attribute.

**4. `test_audit_prescan.js` gains 20 new cases** (no second test file — this is the file the spec said to
find, and it already covers `prescanStaticPages()`): a true negative on the real 2,181-page surface, one
isolated positive control per sub-rule, an all-three-fire test pinned at exactly 3 (never 1, never a
suspect-per-link flood), two coupling proofs (home.html, planner.js), an entity-decoding pin, three
degrade-safety cases, and an `AUDIT_STATIC_PAGES`-disables-prescan assertion.

## The rule that carries the weight (same one 169 shipped)

> **Reuse before inventing.** A second hardcoded copy of the router's param list *is* the exact bug class
> this signal exists to catch.

`extractQuotedArray()` and `loadRouterAllowedParams()` are reused **verbatim** from 169, not reimplemented
— `grep` for a literal `'token'`/`'poolTypes'` array anywhere in the new code finds nothing. The one place
this item genuinely couldn't reuse 169's own mechanism — `/plan.html` links, where the IA router never
arbitrates at all — is resolved the same way, not by inventing an allow-list: `loadPlannerAllowedParams()`
scans `planner.js` for its own `urlParams.get('<key>')` call sites, so the check can never drift out of
sync with what the planner actually reads.

## Proving the coupling is live, not decorative

Two dedicated tests point the loaders at a **copied fixture with one param appended**, live, and show a
link using that param flip from suspect to clean:

- `home.html` fixture: append `'zzzCustomParam'` to `ANALYTICS_PARAMS` → a `?zzzCustomParam=1` home-path
  link flips suspect → clean.
- `planner.js` fixture: append a `urlParams.get('zzzPlannerParam')` call site → a `/plan.html?zzzPlannerParam=1`
  link flips suspect → clean.

Both ran for real, both passed.

## Non-vacuity — three neuter cycles, real transcripts

Each cycle: neuter one sub-rule's own decision line → run the full test file → confirm ONLY that
sub-rule's cases go red → restore from a saved golden copy → confirm `md5sum` matches → confirm green
again.

| cycle | neutered | cases lost | cases kept green |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 (rule a) | `urlQueryKeys(suffix).filter(k => !allowed.has(k))` → `&& false` | **7** (both positive controls, the cap test, both coupling proofs, the all-three test dropping 3→2, the planner-degrade test) | all rule (b)/(c)-only cases |
| 2 (rule b) | the final `badTargets.length > 0` check → `&& false` | **6** (all 3 positive controls, the all-three test dropping to 2, the home.html-degrade test, the unreadable-page test whose fixture happens to be rule-b-shaped) | all rule (a)/(c)-only cases |
| 3 (rule c) | `!ownedPathResolvesToFile(linkPath)` → `&& false` | **3** (the positive control, the all-three test, the home.html-degrade test) | all rule (a)/(b)-only cases |

All three restores verified byte-identical against the same golden md5
(`c4e93b8ffccf2f8b53d4a13b7a243431`), each followed by a full green re-run (29/29). Full transcripts in
`172-notes.md`.

## Deviations, disclosed (full list in `172-notes.md`)

- **The spec's own evidence table says "2,183" pages; the real scanned count is 2,181.** `listLeafPages()`
  (unchanged) excludes each directory's own `index.html`; `2094 + 89 = 2183` counts those two index pages,
  which are never actually scanned. A ticket, not a fix — `listLeafPages()` is out of scope here.
- **No pre-029 commit was reachable** for rule (b)'s positive control (this checkout is a 50-commit
  shallow clone whose oldest commit postdates item 029 by ~112 items) — the spec explicitly permits a
  fixture fallback in that case, used and disclosed rather than silently substituted.
- **`prescanStaticPages()` gained `opts.pages`/`opts.homeHtml`/`opts.plannerJs`** — the same test-support
  override convention 169 already shipped for `prescanTextSurfaces()`'s `opts.files`/`opts.homeHtml`, not
  a new mechanism. With no opts, behaviour is provably unchanged.

## Scope and safety

`git diff --name-only`: `audit-app.js`, `test_audit_prescan.js` (plus `product-loop-kit/signals/audit-findings.json`,
a `DEFAULT_OUT` artifact any `node audit-app.js` run legitimately overwrites — same disclosure 171 made
for its own session). No product file, generator, generated page, sitemap, or OG asset touched.
`git diff -S APY_SANITY_LIMIT` / `-S DEFAULT_MIN_TVL` both empty — no trust rail moved; this only *adds* a
check. `package.json` byte-identical (`dependencies`/`devDependencies` compared structurally, not by eye).
`telegram-bot/`, `whatsapp-bot/`, `workers/` untouched.

All 8 `require('./audit-app.js')` test files in the repo were run individually and are green:
`test_audit_prescan.js` (29/29), `test_audit_text_surfaces.js` (32/32, unaffected — separate signal map),
`test_audit_app.js` (3/3), `test_seo_surface_audit.js` (5/5), `test_audit_pool_prescan.js` (14/14),
`test_audit_runner.js` (9 assertions), `test_audit_planner_surface.js` (9/9),
`test_audit_planner_flow.js` (11/11). `node run-tests.js --lane=plain`: 36/36.

## What was NOT run

The full browser lane (`node run-tests.js --lane=browser`, ~64 files) — exceeds the 5-minute foreground
timebox by a wide margin (163/169/170/171's own precedent: ~30min serial). All 8 of the lane's
audit-consuming files were run individually instead (all green, above) — the same substitute 171-notes.md
used. The remaining ~56 non-audit browser-lane files were not re-verified individually; none of them read
`PRESCAN_SIGNALS`/`prescanStaticPages`/`home.html`'s router arrays/`planner.js`'s `urlParams.get()` sites
per `run-tests.js`'s own transitive-require classification, so risk is low but is an inference, not a
direct observation.

## Instrumentation

**None** — loop tooling under the 2026-07-23 pre-traffic mandate, disclosed per the
142/149/154/155/160/169/171 precedent.

## Quiz

1. Rule (a)'s allowed query-key set is not one fixed list. What determines which set applies to a given
   link, and why can a `/plan.html` link never be checked against `home.html`'s router arrays?
2. The spec explicitly forbids validating `?pool=<id>` liveness against `data/pools-snapshot.json`. What
   would happen if this item had used it anyway, and why?
3. Rules (a) and (c) share one `matchAll(HTML_HREF_RE)` pass; rule (b) runs its own separate pass. Why
   can't rule (b) reuse the same pass as (a)/(c)?
4. Neutering rule (c) alone also turns the "UNREADABLE home.html degrades safely" test red — a test whose
   headline claim is about rule (a)'s behaviour. Why is that a real interaction and not a bug in either
   the test or the neuter?
5. `link-target-integrity` is P1, while `broken-number-literal`/`absurd-magnitude` are P0. Both describe a
   generated page telling a reader something untrue. What distinguishes them?
